text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The newspaper prints a report on "the results of the economic mission to Japan", which involved representatives of 40 Romanian banks and companies.
- The Metanef foreign trade company signed a contract in Japan on Tuesday for the export of $13 million worth of steel plates produced by the Sidex steel plant in Galati.
ADEVARUL ECONOMIC
- Interviews with Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu, politicians and businessmen, on the bill of domestic investors.
- The newspaper runs a draft proposal on the restructuring of the non-ferous mining sector.
- Trends on the Romanian detergents market -- a newspaper report shows that Romanians favour foreign brands.
ADEVARUL
- Romania has to pay $2.0 billion from the budget for the 96 Dracula helicopters produced by Bell Helicipter in Brasov, the newspaper says.

- A newspaper survey of several major Romanian companies shows that company managers say a rate of 8,000 lei per dollar would encourage exports, and that the present exchange rate is "overvalued" against the greenback.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Renel electricity authority has asked the Industry Ministry to cut subsidies on the price for domestic power consumption.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania eyes $1.0 billion worth of investments in the telecommunications sector this year, the newspaper quotes Communications Minister Sorin Pantis as saying.
General:
- A former Comunist-era Secutitate secret police officer has been appointed head of the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI), in charge of Western Romania, the newspaper says.
- After a six-year delay, the government adopted the bill of public officials, dubbed "the anti-tips" bill.
- Defence Minister Victor Babiuc has asked for higher defence budget outlays, saying that his sector needs more money after Romania's failure to gain early admission to NATO.
- Communications Minister Sorin Pantis said that Romanian cable operators will be allowed to broadcast news to the country's two million cable television subscribers.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Defence Minister Victor Baniuc said Romania would boost military ties with Russia.
- Romania will import aurochs, a rare and fabled species of buffaloes which used to roam in the forests of northern Moldova in the Middle Ages. $ = 7,148 lei
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
